explanation: Méliès found that stopping the camera mid-shot could make people vanish or transform, and built his films on such tricks. Ben Kingsley played him in Martin Scorsese's Hugo (2011).

claims.text: Georges Méliès, a former stage magician, made A Trip to the Moon (1902).
In A Trip to the Moon, a capsule fired from a giant cannon lands in the eye of the Man in the Moon.
Louis Lumière, Abel Gance and Jean Renoir did not make A Trip to the Moon.
Méliès used stop tricks, halting the camera mid-shot, to make people vanish or change on screen.
Ben Kingsley played Georges Méliès in Martin Scorsese's Hugo (2011).
